writeup: TIC 257747010 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 4.234848 days, identified through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a 25.38% dimming, while a secondary eclipse was detected at 5.7 sigma significance. Pixel-level difference imaging confirms the signal originates from the target location, with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 112.4. However, data quality analysis reveals that alternating eclipses differ significantly in depth, suggesting the initial period estimate was half the true value. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel find, though the machine-learning screening score of 0.45 indicates moderate confidence in its validity as a real eclipsing system.
